correctness.rationale: The final claim is exactly u(K)=2 (crossing changes only; virtual Reidemeister/detours cost zero) for Green knots 5.40, 5.107, 5.880, 5.1238 represented by their specified source signed Gauss codes, not an all-five-crossing classification. Independently transcribed all four primary Appendix 6.2 10-token signed codes. Their chord endpoint parities give odd crossings {1,2,4,5} and negative signs on all four, so J=-4 in each code. Kauffman Theorem 2 establishes J is invariant under virtual isotopy; one classical crossing change swaps arrow O/U and sign but leaves chord endpoints/parity fixed, changing J by at most 2; unknot has J=0, so u>=2. Independently implemented code transforms crossings 1 and 4 and verifies each Gauss-code RII cancellation has adjacent over endpoints, adjacent under endpoints and opposite signs and RI has adjacent opposite O/U endpoints. For 5.40/5.107: RII(4,5), RI(3), RII(1,2); for 5.880/5.1238: RII(1,2), RI(3), RII(4,5). All four end with empty code and thus u<=2, proving equality. Independently computed canonical source tree sha exactly. This is a complete finite diagram proof and is not mere package VERIFY_OK.
residual_risks: Gauss-code proofs use the conventional signed O/U Reidemeister RI and RII moves; no claim is made about arbitrary virtual knots whose crossing-change number may be infinite.
Only these four Green-labeled knot types and their transcribed published codes are covered; the 2026 table may contain other unresolved rows.
No independent visual knot diagram drawing was needed beyond verified Gauss-code move criteria; static finite check independently replayed all changes.

value.rationale: The crossing-change unknotting number is a natural exact invariant for named low-complexity virtual knots. The newest focused published table visibly leaves each of these four Green entries unresolved at u<=2, with slice-genus intervals [1,2]. Establishing a matching two-move obstruction for a uniform four-entry motif gives directly reusable exact knot-table values and distinguishes them from a possible one-change knot; future knot-table comparisons require precisely these entries. This is small finite mathematical work, not a claim of a new method or a general theorem. Its value is confined to making four explicit non-exact published entries exact using an independently checkable code calculation.
residual_risks: Modest contribution: very short application of established odd writhe and known upper-bound data.
